strongest_objection: The declared type is narrower than the map it heads. The of-sentence promises mechanisms by which the real time until one can no longer meet obligations differs from what cash over burn predicts, and six of the eighteen items do not literally do that. Near the pole's own example gives the shop and the startup 'the same three months': the cash figure predicts the time correctly, and what it misreads is the runway's response to a cut. Burn you cannot put down ('unequal runways under cuts') and Reach the cliff (the runway's worth is a step in its length) are likewise about the derivative or the value of the runway, not its length. Stamp's clock, The back and Runway in shots are deaths that are not failures to meet an obligation but the end of the undertaking in a unit money does not buy. These are the strongest items in the map, so the repair is to the type, not to the members: 'Mechanisms by which a person's or a firm's real time until it must stop, or what that time is worth, or how it answers to the operator's own moves, differs from what its cash balance over its burn predicts, each named with the carrier that holds the difference, what the cash figure misreads, and whether a better count corrects it or only a change in what is counted.' With that widening the type has a plausible member (Date bomb), a tempting nonmember (stretching payables, which moves the figure rather than misreading it), and every item satisfies it. The secondary faults are two modality overclaims (Forbearance clock asserts the creditor's trouble coincides with yours unconditionally; Too expensive to let die says a dying creditor keeps you alive anyway, when a creditor in receivership has no future in which replacement cost matters), one blurred fork (naturalization listed as a cash-like cliff when a permission arriving on a date is Stamp's clock read upward), and one seriation misplacement (Any-town skill is filed under quantities in no monetary unit while its own correction is priced in wages).

items.item: Date bomb: an obligation that arrives as a step rather than a slope, as the lease that renews in September, the annual premium, the tax bill in April, the tuition due before the school year, so the death is at the first step the balance cannot clear and not at the month the average burn predicts; the carrier is the calendar, the cash figure misreads a staircase as a ramp, and a better count corrects it, since the schedule was always on paper; the seasonal case, the fisherman's winter or the nine-month salary, is the same staircase repeated.
items.why: Tested as the closest neighbor of Reach the cliff; the carrier, misread and correction are identical (calendar, staircase as ramp, count to the date) and the author's seriation note concedes 'the same calendar read up and down'. It survives because the two produce opposite actions under a cut, which is a difference in what the operator does, not in wording; but that difference lives in the value of the runway, not its length, which is why the type sentence must widen.

items.item: Reach the cliff: an asset that arrives as a step, as the vesting date, the pension's twentieth year, the bonus paid in March, the tranche released on a milestone, naturalization at year five, so the runway is not a number of months but a race whose prize is a jump, and the whole loss is quitting three weeks early; the carrier is the payer's schedule, the cash figure misreads a binary as a slope, since the months before the cliff are worth nothing on their own and everything as a bridge; not Date bomb, which is a step down, and the correction is counting to the date, not counting months.
items.why: Two faults. Naturalization at year five is a permission arriving on a date, not an asset arriving as cash; it is Stamp's clock read upward and its presence here blurs the fork the map draws at Date bomb → Stamp's clock, where the whole question is whether cash converts to time. And the discriminator 'not Date bomb, which is a step down, and the correction is counting to the date, not counting months' names the same correction Date bomb has, so it does not separate; what separates them is that a step down is cleared by having cash at the date while a step up is raced for by spending whatever reaches the date, so a cut that lengthens months and misses the date is a loss.
items.repair: Reach the cliff: an asset that arrives as a step, as the vesting date, the pension's twentieth year, the bonus paid in March, the tranche released on a milestone, so the runway's worth is a step in its length, a race whose prize is a jump, and the whole loss is quitting three weeks early; the carrier is the payer's schedule, the cash figure misreads a binary as a slope, since the months before the cliff are worth nothing on their own and everything as a bridge; the same calendar as Date bomb read upward, and distinct in what it makes the operator do, since a step down is cleared by having the cash at the date while a step up is raced for by spending whatever reaches the date, so a cut that lengthens the months and misses the date is a loss and not a gain; a permission that arrives on a date, as naturalization at year five, is Stamp's clock read upward and not this.

items.item: Near the pole: runway is cash over net burn, and net burn is the difference of two large flows, so two operators with identical months differ by how close their burn sits to the pole where income covers it, as a shop taking in ninety and spending a hundred has the same three months as a startup taking in nothing and spending ten, and only the shop can multiply its runway by a ten-percent cut; the carrier is the ratio of the gross flows to their difference, the cash figure misreads a point for the steepness of the curve the point sits on, and counting corrects it, but only if the gross flows are counted and not the net.
items.why: The best item in the first grade and the map's near priority, kept as written; it does not fit the type as declared, since both operators' real time is exactly what cash over burn says, and the fix is the widened of-sentence in the strongest objection rather than a change to the item. The arithmetic checks: a ten-percent cut takes the shop's net burn to zero and the startup's from ten to nine.

items.item: Forbearance clock: a debt with no schedule, as the family loan, the supplier who lets the invoice slide, the tax authority that has not yet noticed, the credit line uncalled, is due at the creditor's discretion, and the creditor's discretion runs on the creditor's own runway, so the debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which is when you are; the carrier is the creditor's clock, the cash figure misreads an uncalled debt as not due, and no count of your own ledger corrects it, since the due date lives in someone else's; Receivable from the dying on the other side of the sheet.
items.why: Modality. 'The debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which is when you are' asserts a correlation as fact; the tax authority's audit cycle and a solvent relative's sudden need are uncorrelated with your weather, and the map's own edge from Receivable from the dying correctly makes the shared weather a condition. The item should carry the same condition rather than promoting it.
items.repair: Forbearance clock: a debt with no schedule, as the family loan, the supplier who lets the invoice slide, the tax authority that has not yet noticed, the credit line uncalled, is due at the creditor's discretion, and the creditor's discretion runs on the creditor's own runway, so the debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which need not be when you are, and is when you are whenever the two of you share weather; the carrier is the creditor's clock, the cash figure misreads an uncalled debt as not due, and no count of your own ledger corrects it, since the due date lives in someone else's; Receivable from the dying on the other side of the sheet.

items.item: Too expensive to let die: a runway carried by the cost of your death to others, as the only doctor in the district, the engineer who alone knows the plant, the tenant whose leaving would empty a building in a bad market, so counterparties who could call the debt do not, because replacing you costs more than carrying you; the carrier is their replacement cost, the cash figure misreads your clock as yours when it is theirs, and it is corrected only by counting what your death costs someone else; not Forbearance clock, which runs on the creditor's health, since a dying creditor who cannot replace you keeps you alive anyway, and not a leverage, since nothing is exercised.
items.why: Modality in the discriminator. 'A dying creditor who cannot replace you keeps you alive anyway' is false at the limit: a creditor in receivership has no future in which to need you, so it has no replacement cost, and its receiver calls every debt. The override of creditor health by replacement cost holds while the creditor expects to survive, and the item should say so; the strange mechanism (a runway held in the creditor's dependence) is preserved, only bounded.
items.repair: Too expensive to let die: a runway carried by the cost of your death to others, as the only doctor in the district, the engineer who alone knows the plant, the tenant whose leaving would empty a building in a bad market, so counterparties who could call the debt do not, because replacing you costs more than carrying you; the carrier is their replacement cost, the cash figure misreads your clock as yours when it is theirs, and it is corrected only by counting what your death costs someone else; not Forbearance clock, which runs on the creditor's health, since a creditor in trouble who cannot replace you keeps you alive for as long as it expects a future in which to need you, though a creditor in receivership has no replacement cost, since it has no future to replace you in, and its receiver calls the debt; and not a leverage, since nothing is exercised.

items.item: Any-town skill: a skill that is cash in any town lengthens the runway to the time it takes to move, while a skill that is cash only here shortens it to the cash, as the nurse or the welder against the fixer who knows this council, the session player known in this scene, the courtier; the carrier is the geography of the market for the skill, the cash figure misreads the pile for the pump, and it is corrected only by counting where the skill sells and at what discount, a change of quantity; adjacent to the floors under income, which the sibling map keeps, and adds only that the floor's location is what sets the clock.
items.why: Two faults. The discriminator leans on 'the sibling map' keeping the floors under income; no such map is in the atlas or in this fleet's corpus directory, and an item's boundary must be stated in the item, not delegated to a record that may never exist. And the item's own correction, 'counting where the skill sells and at what discount', is a count in wages, so the seriation's claim that it sits among quantities in no monetary unit is wrong; the mechanism is a count of a market you are not in, which is the second grade's kind of counting.
items.repair: Any-town skill: a skill that is cash in any town lengthens the runway to the time it takes to move, while a skill that is cash only here shortens it to the cash, as the nurse or the welder against the fixer who knows this council, the session player known in this scene, the courtier; the carrier is the geography of the market for the skill, the cash figure misreads the pile for the pump, and it is corrected only by counting where the skill sells and at what discount, which is a count of a market you are not yet in; not a floor under income, which is what the skill fetches, since here only where it fetches it matters, and the location of the floor is what sets the clock.

items.item: Runway in shots: for anyone who must find a thing before the cash ends, a founder's product, a scientist's result, an actor's part, a prospector's seam, the runway is not months but trials, so halving the burn doubles the months and may leave the shots unchanged if the cut removed the trial capacity, and the same firm with three months is short at one shot a month and long at ten; the carrier is the trial rate, the cash figure misreads time for attempts, and the correction is a change of unit, not a better count; the last item on the route because here the clock is not time at all.
items.why: The clause 'the last item on the route because here the clock is not time at all' writes the item's list position into its own text, which the practice forbids (item identities, not positions, are the endpoints); the mechanism is sound and its modality is honestly carried in the limits. The arithmetic checks: with any fixed burn, a cut to trial burn lengthens months and shortens total shots, so the item and its edge agree.
items.repair: Runway in shots: for anyone who must find a thing before the cash ends, a founder's product, a scientist's result, an actor's part, a prospector's seam, the runway is not months but trials, so halving the burn doubles the months and may leave the shots unchanged if the cut removed the trial capacity, and the same firm with three months is short at one shot a month and long at ten; the carrier is the trial rate, the cash figure misreads time for attempts, and the correction is a change of unit, not a better count; here the clock is not time at all, so no count in months, however good, touches it.

neighbor_test.left: Date bomb: an obligation that arrives as a step rather than a slope, as the lease that renews in September, the annual premium, the tax bill in April, the tuition due before the school year, so the death is at the first step the balance cannot clear and not at the month the average burn predicts; the carrier is the calendar, the cash figure misreads a staircase as a ramp, and a better count corrects it, since the schedule was always on paper; the seasonal case, the fisherman's winter or the nine-month salary, is the same staircase repeated.
neighbor_test.right: Reach the cliff: an asset that arrives as a step, as the vesting date, the pension's twentieth year, the bonus paid in March, the tranche released on a milestone, naturalization at year five, so the runway is not a number of months but a race whose prize is a jump, and the whole loss is quitting three weeks early; the carrier is the payer's schedule, the cash figure misreads a binary as a slope, since the months before the cliff are worth nothing on their own and everything as a bridge; not Date bomb, which is a step down, and the correction is counting to the date, not counting months.
neighbor_test.separating_case: A firm with thirty in cash and a burn of ten, so three months on the figure. Case A: a lease renewal of twenty falls at month two; the balance of ten cannot clear it and the firm dies at month two, earlier than the figure says, and the cure is to cut burn so that twenty is in hand at the date. Case B: a tranche of twenty is released at month four; the figure's three months are correct and the cliff is missed, unless the firm borrows ten at any rate to reach month four, in which case it lives, so the cure is to spend or borrow whatever reaches the date, and a burn cut that lengthens the months past three but still misses month four is worthless. The two separate in what the operator does under a cut, cut for the bomb and race for the cliff, and that is a real difference; but they collapse in carrier, misread and correction, and the separation lives in the worth of the runway rather than its length, which is exactly the dimension the declared type omits. Repair rather than merge, with the type widened.

boundary_case: Stretching payables: paying every vendor thirty days later 'extends the runway', and operators say so. Out, because the cash figure moves when you do it; the balance really is higher and the months really are longer, so nothing is misread. The two parts of it that are mechanisms are already in the map: the creditor who tolerates the stretch is Forbearance clock, and the stretch that is seen and repriced is Watched burn. The ruling also confirms the map's implicit rule, which the of-sentence should carry and the author's own boundary case relies on: the figure is assumed right, and the question is what a right figure still misreads.

seriation.note: The axis has real endpoints (a calendar the operator already owns; a clock that is not time) and the hinge adjacency, Hurry discount → Watched burn, teaches: the hurried sale is the last illusion solvable inside one's own books and also the act by which the books become visible, so counting better tips into counting what others count. One misplacement: Any-town skill sits in the third grade, quantities in no monetary unit, but its own correction is a count of wages in another town, a market you are not in, which is second-grade counting. Move it to follow Weakest wallet and precede The back; the second turn then becomes Any-town skill → The back, the last carrier priced in money against the first that money does not buy, which is cleaner than the current Weakest wallet → The back and should be recorded in seriation.note. Reach the cliff beside Date bomb is defended by the separating case above once the type is widened.

edges.why: The antecedent 'if the creditor's own clock is short' is unbounded, and the consequent 'replacement cost overrides the creditor's health' fails at the limit the antecedent includes: a creditor that has actually died has no future in which to need you, so a receiver calls the debt regardless of how hard you are to replace. The dependency the edge should show is that the runway moved into the creditor's dependence is bounded by the creditor's own survival.
edges.repair_label: If the creditor's own clock is short but not out and you cannot be replaced, the forbearance outlives the creditor's trouble, since replacement cost overrides the creditor's health for as long as the creditor expects a future in which to need you; past the creditor's own death the override fails, a receiver has no replacement cost, and the runway that had moved from the creditor's ledger to the creditor's dependence ends with the creditor, so the operator who raises the cost of their own death has bought time bounded by the creditor's.

edges.why: Tested: the antecedent fails for an operator whose books are private and whose pile sells through a broker who does not know the seller's clock, and then the discount has a fixed point inside one ledger; when the antecedent holds the sale is itself the signal and the fixed point moves. A real loop a sequence conceals, since the two items sit in different grades of the route.

Tested arithmetically: with any fixed burn, cutting trial burn raises months and lowers total shots, so the two units disagree as claimed; the closing clause, that a firm at breakeven with no trials has an infinite runway and no way to arrive, is the sharpest sentence in the map and is a real incompatibility between units, not a restatement of the sequence.

modality_problems: Forbearance clock states 'which is when you are' as fact; the correlation between creditor's and debtor's trouble is a condition (shared weather), which the edge from Receivable from the dying already carries and the item should too.

Too expensive to let die's discriminator says a dying creditor who cannot replace you keeps you alive anyway; a creditor in receivership has no replacement cost because it has no future, so the claim must be bounded by the creditor's own survival.
Reach the cliff lists naturalization at year five among assets that arrive as a step; a permission arriving on a date is not cash and sits on the Stamp's clock side of the map's own fork.
Any-town skill's boundary is delegated to 'the sibling map' keeping floors under income; no such record exists in the atlas, so the boundary was an unsupported reference rather than a stated limit.

The of-sentence's 'meet its obligations' is narrower than the map: Near the pole, Burn you cannot put down and Reach the cliff concern the runway's response or worth rather than its length, and Stamp's clock, The back and Runway in shots concern deaths that are not defaults; the widened type in the strongest objection resolves this without touching the items' modality.
Runway in shots is correctly marked speculative in generality in the limits; no promotion found. The two loops are correctly marked analytical.
duplication: None. The baseline this map corrects is exactly one item of clocks-that-are-not-clocks, Larder countdown (a stock consumed at a rate reads as time remaining), and every item here is a way that reading misreads; that is adjacency by construction, not duplication, and the boundary_claim already names it. Watched burn is adjacent to that list's Queue clock (a reflexive reading) and Forbearance clock to its Contract calendar; where-margin-hides' Supplier's clock and Float are the firm-side mirror of Forbearance clock (collecting before paying) and are margin mechanisms, not clock illusions; pivot-invariants lists 'The health of the operator' as a retained asset where The back names the mechanism by which producing income spends it. No item restates the business-adjacent lists named in the brief.
best_unresolved_seed: Lead-time floors: the last months of a runway are spent buying the next one, a raise that takes six months, a job hunt, a move, so a death line sits above zero drawn by a counterparty's latency rather than by the wind-down bill. Cost of the coffin has the floor (drawn by the cost of stopping), Any-town skill has the move time (a runway lengthened to the time it takes to relocate), and Watched burn has the investor who waits, but nothing in the map holds the general mechanism that a runway must contain the time it takes to replace itself, that this time is set by someone else's decision cycle, and that it is the floor operators actually die on ('you are dead at six months, not zero'). It would sit in the second grade beside Watched burn, and the probe is small: for ten firms that raised, subtract the days from first pitch to wire from the months of runway they reported at first pitch, and see how many were already below zero.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after widening the item type to cover the runway's worth and its response to cuts, repairing five items (two modality overclaims in Forbearance clock and Too expensive to let die, a blurred fork in Reach the cliff, a delegated boundary in Any-town skill, a positional clause in Runway in shots), relabeling one edge so the creditor's-dependence runway is bounded by the creditor's survival, and moving Any-town skill out of the non-monetary grade.
